Download the latest version from the thread here: Ancile v1.10

Changes (See the "changes.txt" files in the "docs" directory for full lists):

  • Completely re-organized the Ancile project
  • Ancile is no longer restricted to Windows 7/8.x
  • Made a number of changes to allow Ancile to be a more general purpose script launcher.
  • Created build scripts so that people can create their own releases
  • Made a few minor changes to various plugins.

 

 

What's new?

Ancile originally started as a fork of th3power's Aegis-voat scripts. My original intention was to just update and maintain those scripts, but over time Ageis has changed and expanded into something that barely resembles those original scripts. It's been a lot of fun and I've really enjoyed making these releases for you, but lately I haven't had a lot of time to update Ancile. Fortunately, I haven't needed to make many major changes to any of Ancile's core functionality or plugins, and Microsoft seems to have slowed down on it's malicious updates.

 

What does this mean?

Because I seem to have less and less time to devote to Ancile, I've made the following changes.

  • I've split Ancile into Ancile Core and it's various plugins. This will allow me to maintain everything separately. Which will make Ancile more modular and easier to maintain, update, and customize.

  • Ancile is now more geared to running plugins rather than to any specific task. The official Ancile release will continue to include approved plugins that remove malicious updates and disable telemetry, but Ancile Core will be available to allow anyone to create a custom release which include plugins that can do anything.

  • Ancile no longer restricts it's execution to WIndows 7/8.x. This is now the responsibility of each individual plugin to check OS version numbers and act accordingly. It's been this way for a while now, but I'm now making it more apparent that Ancile will work for Windows 7 (probably Vista too) and above.

  • I've created a set of build scripts that will allow anyone to generate a custom release of Ancile. This helps me to maintain an official Ancile release, and if anyone wants to build their own version of Ancile, I hope they find this helpful.

 

Is this the end of Ancile?

Not yet. I'll continue to release the official Ancile release when i can, and I'll do my best to keep important data files updated. While I do have less time to devote to Ancile's development, I feel that it's in a good place for that slowdown. Ancile Core does what it needs to, the default plugins included with the official release function as expected (for the most part), and plugins can auto update their data files on each run.
